lines: The sleeves hang uncertainly at summer’s end
On the early‑morning train I swayed and remembered
That nostalgic scenery
Repeating countless detours
The same kind of town simply passed by
My reflection appears in the window
I wonder if you’re still there just as you were then
We raced around on that bent, warped bicycle
A foolish tightrope act, blood seeping onto my knees
Now I feel a terrible emptiness
No matter how much our heights may change
May there be something that never changes
Encouraged by a trivial memory
I keep singing, I keep singing, I keep singing
La‑la‑la‑la, la‑la‑la‑la, la‑la‑la‑la
Taxis rush through the busy streets
Still vaguely shouldered along
I sneezed
I stare out the window
In that moment my heart truly trembled
I strongly wish we could meet again
I will never forget
I wonder if you’re still there just as you were then
I dropped one shoe in the thicket and searched for it
“No matter what happens, we’ll surely make it work,”
I remember the days when we could laugh innocently
Even if I’m wounded in the most clumsy way
A bouquet for the endless days
Chasing that trivial memory
I keep singing, I keep singing, I keep singing
La‑la‑la‑la, la‑la‑la‑la, la‑la‑la‑la
The waning moon before sunrise
I wonder if you’re watching it somewhere too
For some reason my chest aches without any reason
A blurred face, a hazy hue
It feels too late to shout that I’m sad now
Perhaps everything was far too late
If I could start walking again from the beginning
I’d want to meet you, even if we pass each other
No matter how much our heights may change
May there be something that never changes
Encouraged by a trivial memory
I keep singing, I keep singing, I keep singing
La‑la‑la‑la, la‑la‑la‑la, la‑la‑la‑la
The waning moon before sunrise
I wonder if you’re watching it somewhere too
The sunrise comes, laughing that there’s nothing
It all began in a shade of blue
